videos.script: Lesson 1 ended with a refusal. Git would not save a commit, because it did not know who you were. That is fixed now, so here is the commit. {{repeat}} But watch what happens before it. Two commands, not one. First git add. Then git commit. {{two}} Everybody asks why. Why not one command that saves the file? {{why}} Because a commit is not a save button. It is a sentence about a change. And most days, the files on your screen hold more than one change. {{mixed}} A fix to the opening hours. A new stylesheet. Something half-written that is not ready. {{three}} Git add is how you choose. You put the pieces that belong together on one side, the staging area, and the commit takes exactly those. Nothing else. {{staging}} So a file can be in three places. In your folder, as you are editing it. Staged, waiting for the next commit. And in the repository, saved for good. {{places}} Git status tells you which is which, every time you ask. This lesson is those three places, and the four commands that move a file between them. {{title}}
